statement.text:
(Well-known problem). A finite group G is called an IYB-group if it is iso-
morphic to the permutation group of a finite involutive non-degenerate set-theoretic
solution of the Yang–Baxter equation, or equivalently, G is isomorphic to the mul-
tiplicative group of a finite left brace. Assume that the Sylow subgroups of a finite
soluble group G are IYB-groups. Is G an IYB-group?             A. Ballester-Bolinches
